info.title: Blendy API
info.description:
Backend for Blendy, a point-of-sale and inventory system for Kenyan retail SMEs.

**Tenancy.** Every tenant-scoped endpoint reads the organization from an `X-Organization` header. Requests without it resolve to no tenant, and the viewsets fail closed — reads return an empty result set and writes are refused.

**Authentication.** JWT bearer tokens from `/api/auth/login/`. Two paths stay open to anonymous callers so guest checkout works: creating a sale and creating a payment against it.

**Pricing.** Prices live on a pricelist, not on the product. Each organization gets a `Default Pricelist` at onboarding, and a sale is priced from it — an organization without one cannot transact.

Bearer.name: Authorization
Bearer.description: JWT access token, as returned by /api/auth/login/. Send it as: Authorization: Bearer <token>

get.summary: Which of the globally defined roles an organization has enabled.
get.description:
This is the only path that links a Role to an Organization. Onboarding
creates the ORG_ADMIN link and registration creates the Viewer one, but
every other role has to be enabled here — so unlike UserRoleAssignmentViewSet
this one cannot simply be made read-only. Without a working create an owner
could never turn on a role beyond those two, and the assignment flow on
/api/users/ would have nothing to offer.

get.summary: Who holds which role, within one organization.
get.description:
UserRoleAssignment carries no organization column of its own: it is tenanted
*transitively*, through organization_role. Inheriting the base scoping was
therefore not merely wrong but inert — its get_queryset filtered on a field
that does not exist, so every request raised FieldError before a single row
was read, and the tenant isolation the base was assumed to be providing was
never actually applied here.

get.summary: Read-only view of the stock ledger.
get.description:
The ledger is append-only and must stay in step with the cached balance on
InventoryItem, so entries are written only through inventory.services. Left
writable, a POST here recorded a movement that changed no stock level, which
is precisely the drift the ledger exists to rule out. Use the restock and
adjust endpoints instead.

post.description:
Send **exactly one** of:

- `quantity` — a signed change, e.g. `-2` for two broken units. Cannot take the balance below zero.
- `counted_quantity` — the figure counted on the shelf. The difference is computed under the row lock that writes it, and a count is authoritative, so it may produce a negative balance.

`reason` is required either way: an unexplained adjustment is what the ledger exists to rule out.

200.description: The counted figure already matched; nothing was written.

400.description: Validation error, or a delta that would take stock below zero.

403.description: Missing X-Organization header, or a cross-tenant reference.

get.summary: US-3: variations at or below the reorder level their owner set.
get.description:
There is no push channel in this deployment (no mail backend, no worker), so
the alert is a queue the owner's dashboard reads, in the same shape as the
pending-payments and unmatched-payments queues.

The threshold is inclusive: MVP test scenario 8 expects selling *down to*
the threshold to fire the alert, not only going under it.

post.description:
Called by Safaricom for money paid straight to the Till, which carries no CheckoutRequestID. The payment is attributed to a tenant by shortcode, then matched to an open sale by payer phone number and amount within a 24-hour window. An ambiguous match — zero candidates or more than one — is queued on `/payments/payments/unmatched/` rather than guessed at.

Always answers 200 in Safaricom's expected shape, including when nothing could be matched, so it stops retrying.

schema.description: Safaricom's C2B confirmation for a direct Till payment.

TransID.description: The M-Pesa receipt. Reconciliation is idempotent on this.

BusinessShortCode.description: Matched against Organization.mpesa_shortcode to attribute the payment.

200.description: Acknowledged. `matched` says whether it landed on a sale.

401.description: Bad token or disallowed source IP.

post.description:
Called by Safaricom, not by your clients. Safaricom does not sign callbacks, so the trust boundary is the secret `token` in the URL plus a source-IP allowlist; the token must match `MPESA_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` and the callback URL registered with Daraja.

A success callback whose amount does not match the payment is never marked paid — it is flagged MISMATCH for review. A failure moves the sale to AWAITING_DIRECT_PAYMENT rather than closing it, so the customer can still pay the Till directly.

schema.description: Safaricom's STK push result callback, forwarded verbatim.

ResultCode.description: 0 means success. Anything else fails the payment and moves the sale to AWAITING_DIRECT_PAYMENT.

Item.description: Flattened by name: Amount, MpesaReceiptNumber, TransactionDate, PhoneNumber.

400.description: Malformed payload. Returned rather than a 500 so Safaricom stops retrying.

401.description: Bad token or disallowed source IP.

404.description: No payment matches the CheckoutRequestID/MerchantRequestID pair.
